scope: Existing eleven source-bound thoracic-disc MRI drafts only; not clinical approval or geometry change

oldTopic.body: Trace a thoracic disc relative to the vertebral endplates and spinal canal. Evaluate its signal and any relation to neural structures on actual MR images.
bullets: A bright or dark atlas material does not reproduce T1, T2 or fluid-sensitive disc appearance.
There are no separate annular tears, nucleus surfaces or validated thoracic nerve roots in this source selection.

newTopic.body: Use the rendered thoracic disc to orient yourself between its source-labelled neighbouring endplates, not as a patient-level marker or MR slice. On actual MRI, establish the level from the localizer and sagittal series using visible landmarks, and confirm that the level is within the acquired coverage.
bullets: Follow the disc margin toward the canal on sagittal images, then correlate the same level on axial images. Assess the disc–canal–cord relationship and surrounding CSF space; check whether the foraminal regions are adequately shown.
Appearance depends on the sequence and image quality. An unacquired or poorly depicted structure is not established as normal; compare the actual images rather than the atlas material colour.

This exterior disc surface supplies no MR signal or verified internal disc layers, cord or thoracic nerve roots. It cannot establish compression, cord signal change or a patient’s exact level. Interpret the actual examination; no scan-to-model registration is supplied.
